title: Household chef or event catering: which arrangement do you need?
body_markdown:
**Choose recurring household cooking for everyday meals, meal preparation for food ready later, and event catering for a single celebration.** This guide helps you decide which arrangement to brief; it is not a ranking of Dubai chefs. For the service itself, start with [myCHEF’s private chef services in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/private-chef-dubai), where you can explore household arrangements and the next steps towards a written proposal.


**TL;DR**

- Recurring household cooking is a continuing arrangement; a one-off dinner is a separate event brief.
- Meal preparation suits food needed later; freshly served meals require cooking days that match your routine.
- Compare responsibilities, grocery arrangements and kitchen access before choosing a schedule.
- myCHEF’s service and pricing pages hold the current household plans and booking information.


## Which chef arrangement fits your home?

Start with what you want to stop managing. That might be dinner after work, several meals prepared ahead, or food and service for one evening with guests. These are different briefs even when they use the same kitchen.

A household chef returns on an agreed schedule. Event catering is arranged around one occasion, with the menu, preparation and service team confirmed for that booking. **The distinction is continuity, not simply the number of guests.**

| Arrangement | Best for | What to clarify | Main trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recurring fresh cooking | Meals served on selected household cooking days | Mealtimes, dishes, booked hours and groceries | The schedule needs to fit when you want to eat |
| Weekly meal preparation | Food prepared for later in the week | Portions, storage, reheating and fridge space | Not every dish works equally well after reheating |
| Fuller household coverage | Several meals and regular kitchen support | Hours, tasks, staffing and handovers | A broader scope needs a more detailed plan |
| Chef-led event catering | One dinner, party or celebration | Menu, guests, service format and clear-down | Event staffing is separate from a recurring household plan |
| Direct chef engagement | A household that wants to manage the arrangement itself | References, scope, payment and replacement | You take responsibility for coordination rather than using a managed service |

## Fresh meals or preparation for later?

Choose freshly served meals when the timing and finish at the table matter. Record when the household eats and what needs to be ready first. A late dinner, children’s earlier meal and lunch for the following day should not be left as an unspoken expectation.

Preparation for later starts with a different question: which meals will you actually use? List office days, meals out and the food already in your fridge before agreeing quantities. Repeating a favourite ingredient can be practical; repeating portions you never eat is not.

Discuss dishes that suit storage and reheating with the chef. Ask for the handling instructions relevant to the actual menu rather than assuming every prepared dish keeps for the same period. For this arrangement, explore [weekly meal preparation in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/weekly-meal-prep-dubai).

## What should go into your household brief?

A useful brief connects preferences to practical work. Include:

- Your Dubai area and access arrangements.
- Who will eat and any differences in portions or mealtimes.
- Preferred cooking days and the meals you need covered.
- Favourite dishes, dislikes and essential dietary requirements.
- Who buys ingredients and how substitutions are approved.
- What the kitchen provides and any equipment limitations.
- Preparation, storage and cleanup responsibilities.

Separate allergies from preferences. Explain the severity and any prescribed dietary instructions before a menu is agreed. myCHEF cannot guarantee a completely allergen-free environment; suitability needs to be discussed against the ingredients and kitchen conditions.

For a more detailed preparation checklist, see [how to prepare your kitchen for a household chef](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/private-chef-kitchen-preparation-dubai).

## Compare the scope before comparing the total

A proposal is useful only when you understand what it covers. Check the cooking hours, frequency, grocery responsibility and any additional staffing. Confirm who coordinates changes and what happens when the regular chef is unavailable.

Use [current household chef pricing and the plan calculator](https://www.mychef.ae/private-chef-dubai/pricing) to compare the live service options. This guide does not replace that rate card or reproduce temporary offers. Grocery costs and other separate items should be clear in your written proposal.

When comparing direct engagement with a managed arrangement, include the work you would handle yourself: checking references, setting the schedule, discussing feedback and arranging cover. Do not assume that an independent chef lacks qualifications or that a managed service is automatically suitable for every home. Assess the actual person and the written responsibilities.

## Planning one dinner instead?

A birthday, anniversary or dinner with friends is an event brief, even if it takes place in your usual kitchen. Explain arrival times, courses, dietary requirements, table service and the time the team can set up and clear down.

Use [event catering in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/catering-dubai) for those arrangements rather than assuming a household visit includes a celebration’s staffing and presentation. Guest count affects the team required; it does not turn a one-off occasion into a recurring chef plan.

## Review the arrangement against your original purpose

After the first visits, ask whether the food is being enjoyed and whether the schedule solves the problem you briefed. Review portions, shopping clarity, kitchen care and what is ready for later. Give concrete feedback: a dish that reheated poorly or a meal time that needs adjusting is more useful than a general request for improvement.



## FAQ


**Should I choose household cooking or event catering?**

Choose household cooking for an agreed recurring schedule and event catering for a single dinner, party or celebration. The distinction is continuity, not just guest count.

**Where can I see current household chef prices?**

The myCHEF household pricing page holds the current service options and plan calculator. Your written proposal confirms the final scope and total.

**Does meal preparation mean daily chef visits?**

No. Preparation visits and freshly served meals are different arrangements. Agree the visit pattern around the dishes, portions and meals your household needs.

**Can household members eat different meals?**

Explain different portions, preferences, mealtimes and dietary requirements in the brief. The proposed menu and available cooking time determine what can be included.

**Are groceries part of the service fee?**

myCHEF household groceries are separate at actual cost. Confirm who shops and any shopping time or direct transport costs in the proposal.

**Is an independent chef always a lower-quality option?**

No. Check the chef’s references, skills and written responsibilities rather than judging quality from the booking model alone. Direct engagement means you manage more of the coordination.

**Can a household chef plan include a birthday dinner?**

Discuss it separately with myCHEF. A one-off celebration uses an event brief, with its menu, staffing and service requirements confirmed for that occasion.


## Your next step

For recurring cooking, send your Dubai area, household size, preferred days and meals. For a celebration, send the date, venue, guest count and service format. **myCHEF’s household service is for a chef who returns; its catering service is for an occasion.**


**Find the right household chef arrangement**

Explore the service, compare current plans and send a clear household brief.
